newsitem.title: GERMANY: Magazine says Nazi crime suspect was Western agent.
newsitem.headline: Magazine says Nazi crime suspect was Western agent.

text.p: A German magazine reported on Sunday that former Nazi SS major Karl Hass worked for Western intelligence while being hunted by war crimes investigators for his part in Italy's worst World War Two massacre.
Der Spiegel said Hass, who is currently detained in Italy, worked for Italian and U.S. agencies until 1953 although he was already wanted in connection with the 1944 massacre.
In the report released ahead of publication on Monday, the news weekly cited an interview it had carried out with Hass and historical documents as the sources for its story.
Der Spiegel said Hass did propaganda work for Americans and spied on communists for Italians. Hass was not immediately contactable to comment on the report.

Italian judges have renewed a detention order against Hass, whose trial is being sought in Italy in connection with the 1944 massacre in which Nazi soldiers shot 335 men and boys in reprisal for a partisan bomb attack.
German justice authorities have also said they want to bring Hass to trial.
Hass has admitted killing two people but said he was under orders and would have been killed if he had refused.
He testified last year at the trial in Rome of fellow former SS officer Erich Priebke, who was charged with war crimes for his role in the massacre.
Priebke was found guilty but freed on the grounds that the statute of limitations on his crimes had elapsed.
